title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: purpose leaf.magic extend R leaflet’s capability use modern icon sets. leaflet::addAwesomeMarkers() exists, core disadvantages; markers fixed size, can one 19 colours, pull icons significantly date icon sets. leaf.magic uses contemporary R packages - currently fontawesome bsicons - access --date SVG icon sets, magick knit onto map markers, leaflet::makeIcon() translate leaflet-usable map marker. core advantages magicIcons() leaflet::awesomeIcons() : Markers pull --date, larger icon sets. Markers icons can colour, can resized. One disadvantage magicIcons() may slower initially create large numbers different icons. However, marker created R session, significantly quicker redraw, closing gap awesomeIcons() magicIcons().

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: document ’ll use -built port_talbot dataset, details location air quality measurement stations around town Port Talbot, Wales, UK, open closed. can give data look using vanilla leaflet:
code:
port_talbot$open_year <- as.integer(format(port_talbot$start_date, "%Y")) port_talbot$popup <- paste0( "", toupper(port_talbot$site), " (", port_talbot$code, ")
Site Type: ", port_talbot$site_type, "
Opened: ", port_talbot$open_year ) leaflet(port_talbot) |> addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |> addMarkers(popup = ~popup)

code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = magicIcons(       icon = "cloud"     )   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: leaf.magic allows vary icons variable. can manually, use one leaf.magic constructor functions like iconFactor(). Note ’s also iconBin() iconQuantile() can help map icons numeric data. case, makes sense choose icons inherent “order” . functions don’t features colorBin() colorQuantile(), part due differences mapping continuous aesthetic like colour discrete aesthetic like icons. nice feature much icon-led - breaks n arguments default length provided icons, don’t need specify ’re happy letting functions decide break-points/probs .
code: site_types <- c("Urban Industrial", "Urban Background", "Urban Traffic")  iconPal <- iconFactor(   icons = c("industry", "house", "car"),   domain = site_types )  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPal(site_type)     )   ) iconPalYr <- iconQuantile(   icons = c("hourglass-start", "hourglass-half", "hourglass-end"),   domain = port_talbot$open_year )  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPalYr(open_year)     )   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: magicIcons() two arguments related colour; markerColor colours tear-drop-shaped marker, iconColor colours icon. hex-code can supplied arguments - either constant value colour values mapped column using leaflet::colorFactor(). markers can set colour, can even use continuous scale (e.g., leaflet::colorNumeric()).
code: catPal <- colorFactor(c("#12436D", "#28A197", "#801650"), port_talbot$site_type)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = catPal(site_type),       iconColor = "#F7F7F7FF"     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = catPal,     values = port_talbot$site_type,     title = "Site Type"   ) palNum <- colorNumeric("viridis", domain = port_talbot$open_year)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPalYr(open_year),       markerColor = palNum(open_year),       iconColor = "white"     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = palNum,     values = port_talbot$open_year,     title = "Opening Year",     labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: Unlike leaflet::awesomeIcons(), magicIcons() can easily re-sized. Much like leaflet::addCircleMarkers(), can vary another variable; let’s make closed sites bit smaller open ones markerSize. Note default 30L, roughly size default leaflet::addMarkers() marker.
code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPal(site_type),       iconColor = "white",       markerSize = ifelse(open, 30L, 20L),       markerColor = catPal(site_type)     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = catPal,     values = port_talbot$site_type,     title = "Site Type"   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}

code: leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPal(site_type),       markerColor = palNum(open_year),       iconColor = "white"     )   ) |>   addLegend(     pal = palNum,     values = port_talbot$open_year,     title = "Opening Year",     labFormat = labelFormat(big.mark = "")   ) |>   addIconLegend(     icons = c("industry", "car", "house"),     labels = site_types,     title = "Site Type"   ) leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(     popup = ~popup,     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = iconPal(site_type),       iconColor = "white",       markerColor = catPal(site_type)     )   ) |>   addIconLegend(     icons = iconPal(site_types),     labels = site_types,     colors = catPal(site_types),     title = "Site Type"   )

title: Getting Started with {leaf.magic}
text: default marker type, “tear-drop” marker, useful instances, may find markers types interest. include circle, square, diamond, heart, star-shaped markers. Additionally, users can specify "none" remove marker entirely, placing icon directly map . Note marker can vary variable, allowing marker style encode extra information.
code: addQuickMarker <- function(map, marker) {   iconColor <- "white"   markerColor <- catPal(port_talbot$site_type)   if (marker == "none") {     iconColor <- markerColor   }   map |>     addMarkers(       popup = ~ popup,       icon = ~ magicIcons(         icon = iconPal(site_type),         iconColor = iconColor,         markerColor = markerColor,         marker = marker       ),       group = marker     ) }  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addQuickMarker("circle") |>   addQuickMarker("square") |>   addQuickMarker("diamond") |>   addQuickMarker("heart") |>   addQuickMarker("star") |>   addQuickMarker("none") |>   addLayersControl(     baseGroups = c("circle", "square", "diamond", "heart", "star", "none"),     options = layersControlOptions(FALSE)   ) |>   addIconLegend(     position = "bottomleft",     icons = iconPal(site_types),     labels = site_types,     colors = catPal(site_types),     title = "Site Type"   ) markPal <- iconFactor(c("circle", "diamond", "square"), site_types)  leaflet(port_talbot) |>   addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>   addMarkers(icon = ~ magicIcons(     marker = markPal(site_type),     markerSize = ifelse(markPal(site_type) == "diamond", 35, 30)   )) |>   addIconLegend(     title = "Site Type",     icons = c("fas fa-circle", "fas fa-diamond", "fas fa-square"),     site_types   )

Try toggling breweries example .
code: cols <- names(awesomePalette)[names(awesomePalette) != "white"]  breweries91$facolor <- sample(cols, nrow(breweries91), replace = TRUE)  breweries91$hexcolor <- unlist(use.names = FALSE, awesomePalette[breweries91$facolor])  leaflet(breweries91) |>   addTiles() |>   addAwesomeMarkers(     icon = ~ awesomeIcons(       icon = "circle",       markerColor = facolor,       iconColor = "#FFFFFF",       library = "fa"     ),     group = "Awesome"   ) |>   addMarkers(     icon = ~ magicIcons(       icon = "fas fa-circle",       markerColor = hexcolor,       iconColor = "#FFFFFF"     ),     group = "Magic"   ) |>   addLayersControl(     baseGroups = c("Awesome", "Magic")   ) leaflet(breweries91) |>   addTiles() |>   addMarkers(icon = magicIcons("beer", "red", "white"), group = "Breweries") |>   addIconAttribution(group = "Breweries") |>   addLayersControl(overlayGroups = "Breweries",                    options = leaflet::layersControlOptions(FALSE))

title: Customisable Icon Markers for leaflet
text: goal leaf.magic overcome somewhat outdated “Font Awesome” implementation vanilla R leaflet constructing markers fly using fontawesome bsicons magick. three issues leaf.magic sets overcome: leaflet::awesomeIcons() limited Font Awesome 4 👎 leaflet::awesomeIcons() limited handful discrete colours 👎 leaflet::awesomeIcons() limited single marker size 👎 Vanilla leaflet doesn’t provide additional features construct legends, icon palettes, like 👎 leaf.magic attempts solve : magicIcons() uses --date versions Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons Icons, powered fontawesome bsicons ✅ magicIcons() uses fontawesome grab marker shape, can therefore colour resize however user desires ✅ leaf.magic exports functions like iconBin() addIconLegend() help developers communicate meanings icons users ✅ leaf.magic thoroughly documented package website, includes getting started guide.

text: magicIcons() allows users use --date Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons icon. addIconLegend() add legend layer leaflet map Font Awesome, Bootstrap, Ionicons icons. iconFactor(), iconBins(), iconQuantile() exist analogues leaflet::colorFactor(), leaflet::colorBins() leaflet::colorQuantile(). awesomePalette provides hex-codes used leaflet::awesomeMarkers(). port_talbot dataset provided demonstrate leaf.magic functionality.
